s1.syndrome_frame: Intermittent confusion and falls in an elderly patient with cardiac history
key_facts: Patient is in their mid-80s
Complaints of intermittent confusion and falls
Medical history of moderate aortic stenosis
Medical history of renal cell carcinoma
Treated with radical nephrectomy, chemotherapy, and radiation
Alert, fully oriented, and in no acute distress on presentation
Heart rate of 89 beats/min
Blood pressure of 127/58 mm Hg
Frequent pauses noted on telemetry
ECG shows atrioventricular block
Intracardiac recordings demonstrate conduction from the atrium through the His-Purkinje system to the ventricle
Prolongation of the His-His interval results in phase IV block within the His-Purkinje system
Echocardiogram shows preserved biventricular systolic function and moderate aortic stenosis

shortlist.label: Atrioventricular Block
shortlist.why_kept: ECG shows atrioventricular block and intracardiac recordings demonstrate conduction abnormalities

shortlist.label: Sick Sinus Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has intermittent confusion and falls, which could be related to cardiac conduction abnormalities

shortlist.label: Adams-Stokes Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has atrioventricular block and symptoms of syncope, which are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Aortic Stenosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a medical history of moderate aortic stenosis, which could be contributing to their symptoms

shortlist.label: Vasovagal Syncope
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has symptoms of syncope and orthostatic hypotension, which could be related to this diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of intermittent confusion and falls, combined with ECG findings of atrioventricular block and frequent pauses noted on telemetry, are consistent with Adams-Stokes Syndrome, which is characterized by episodes of syncope and near-syncope due to transient complete heart block.

rejected.label: Atrioventricular Block
rejected.why: While the patient has atrioventricular block, this is a symptom rather than a diagnosis that explains the full clinical picture.

rejected.label: Sick Sinus Syndrome
rejected.why: There is no evidence of sinus node dysfunction, which is the hallmark of Sick Sinus Syndrome.

rejected.label: Aortic Stenosis
rejected.why: Although the patient has moderate aortic stenosis, this does not directly explain the symptoms of intermittent confusion and falls.

rejected.label: Vasovagal Syncope
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and ECG findings are not consistent with vasovagal syncope, which typically involves a sudden drop in heart rate and blood pressure in response to a trigger.
